newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: COMMENT DEADLINE ON S.AFRICAN LIQUOR LAW EXTENDED.
newsitem.headline: COMMENT DEADLINE ON S.AFRICAN LIQUOR LAW EXTENDED.

text.p: The Department of Trade and Industry on Thursday gave in to demands to extend the deadline for public comment on its controversial new liquor law.
It said in a statement that it had decided to extend the period for comment to September 12 from the original closing date of August 8.
"The DTI wishes to ensure that all interested parties have adequate opportunity to comment," it said.
Liquor Traders' Forum members on Monday staged a protest in Pretoria about the proposed new bill and demanded that the deadline be extended.
They claimed the proposed new law was "absolutely irresponsible" as it would open liquor trading to supermarkets and give minors easy access to alcohol.

The members handed a memorandum to Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin which also alleged that the bill did not address the difficulties faced by shebeen and tavern owners and would entrench the monopoly of big companies.

Last week South African Breweries Ltd (SAB) -- the world's fourth largest brewer which controls 97 percent of the local beer market -- slammed key aspects of the bill as "inappropriate and practical".
Analysts say the bill may force SAB to divest its 30 percent stake in wine and spirits wholesalers Stellenbosch Farmers Winery Ltd (SFW).
